mainTopic: Mistaken rulings: רבי מאיר's penalty, eye blemishes after death, and when an erring judge or examiner must pay
overview: This amud moves through several connected topics about mistaken rulings. First, the גמרא shows from the wording of the משנה that רבי מאיר forbids a בכור slaughtered without an expert as a קנס, a penalty. It then asks whether all eye blemishes change after death, and proves from רבי יאשיה's words that only some do. Next it shows that the unnamed משנה about a non-expert's ruling can fit everyone's view. A ברייתא sets his payment at a quarter for a small animal and half for a large one, and the גמרא explains why. A new משנה teaches that a judge who rules wrongly pays from his own money unless he is a מומחה לבית דין. The גמרא explains that this is a case where the judge caused the loss directly with his own hands, so it does not depend on רבי מאיר's view of דינא דגרמי. Then comes the story of רבי טרפון's mistaken ruling about a cow whose womb was removed, and רבי עקיבא's two reasons why he does not pay. The amud ends as a new משנה begins about a paid examiner of firstborn animals.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה shows רבי מאיר is imposing a penalty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the exact words of רבי מאיר in the משנה, 'since it was slaughtered not by an expert,' and concludes that his ruling is a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה's wording also supports this. רבי מאיר says: 'Since it was slaughtered without an expert's ruling, it is forbidden.' This shows that רבי מאיר is giving a penalty. Yes, this is proven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from the wording of the משנה: רבי מאיר's ruling is a קנס, a penalty for slaughtering without asking an expert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר does not say 'because we can no longer tell whether the blemish is real.' He says 'since it was slaughtered without an expert,' which focuses on the wrong act of the owner. That wording shows the animal is forbidden as a penalty, not because of doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה is also precise; its wording supports this point
An expert who is allowed to judge whether a בכור's blemish permits it
A penalty the רבנן impose
Learn from this; it is proven

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's prohibition here is a קנס. It punishes slaughtering without an expert. It is not caused by doubt about the blemish.

phrases.english: The Mishnah is also precise (and supports this),
Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְנִשְׁחַט שֶׁלֹּא עַל פִּי מוּמְחֶה
phrases.english: since it was slaughtered not according to an expert's ruling,
it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ קְנָסָא קָא קָנֵיס רַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: Learn from this: Rabbi Meir is imposing a penalty.
Indeed, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the explanation given just before this section, that רבי מאיר's ruling is a penalty.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר forbids the animal as a קנס
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of the משנה: 'הואיל ונשחט שלא על פי מומחה'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי מאיר's prohibition is a penalty for slaughtering without an expert.

steps.title: Do all eye blemishes change after death, or only some?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'because of those that change' means: do all eye films change after death, or only some?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: when it says 'because of those that change,' does it mean that all of them change? Or maybe some change and some don't?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the rule that eye blemishes cannot be judged after death because they change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reason was that eye blemishes are not trusted after slaughter 'because they change.' The question is whether this is true of every eye blemish, or only of some of them.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them; an open question in the בית המדרש
Those that change (here, change in appearance after death)
Perhaps

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
"Because of those that change"
phrases.notes: This quotes the earlier reason why eye blemishes can't be judged once the animal is dead.

phrases.english: does it mean that all of them change,
or perhaps there are some that change
and there are some that do not change?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי מאיר's penalty to a new question about how eye blemishes behave after death.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether every eye blemish changes after death or only some

steps.title: What practical difference does the question make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this question matters in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the practical result of the question. It is setting up the next step, which explains the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the גמרא tries to answer the question, it wants to know whether the answer would change any practical ruling. The next step gives that practical difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference?

phrases.english: For what does it make a difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the question in step 2 matters.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical result of the question

steps.title: The difference: whether we can believe witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The difference is about witnesses who say the animal had the same eye blemish while it was alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: It matters for contradicting witnesses. If all eye blemishes change, such witnesses are liars. If some change and some don't, we can rely on them. So what is the answer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the question decides whether we believe witnesses who say this exact blemish was there while the animal was alive. It then asks again for the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every eye blemish changes after death, the blemish we see now cannot match how it looked in life. So witnesses who say it looked the same must be lying. If only some change, their testimony could be true, and we may rely on it.

keyTerms.meaning: To contradict (disprove) witnesses
Liars
We rely on them

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a fact about nature can decide whether a בית דין accepts testimony.

phrases.english: For contradicting witnesses.
phrases.notes: These are witnesses who say the animal had this exact eye blemish while it was still alive.

phrases.english: If you say all of them change,
they are liars;
and if you say there are some that change
and there are some that do not change,
we rely on them.
So what is the answer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'what difference does it make' question, then asks again for the answer to step 2. Step 5 gives that answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question decides whether witnesses who say the blemish existed in life are believed.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה's words show that only some eye blemishes change
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports that רבי יאשיה offered to show him the eye films that change. This implies that some do not change.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבה בר בר חנה said: רבי יאשיה from אושא told me, 'Come and I will show you the eye films that change.' Since he said 'come and I will show you,' this implies that some change and some don't.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a proof from what רבי יאשיה said to רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every eye film changed, there would be nothing special to point out. Offering to show 'the ones that change' means there are others that do not. So witnesses who say the blemish was there in life can be relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: He told me
The thin films/membranes of the eye where these blemishes appear
By implication; we can infer

steps.whatToRemember: Not all eye blemishes change after death. Some change and some don't, so witnesses about the blemish in life are not automatically liars.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
for Rabba bar bar Chana said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׂח לִי רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה דְּמִן אוּשָׁא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya from Usha told me:
Come and I will show you the eye films that change.
Since he said to him "Come and I will show you,"
it follows that there are some that change
and there are some that do not change.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the open question from step 2 and step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That only some eye blemishes change after death
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יאשיה's words to רבה בר בר חנה: 'בא ואראך בדוקין שהן משתנים'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Some eye blemishes change and some don't, so such witnesses can be relied on.

steps.title: Does the unattributed משנה follow only רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a non-expert whose ruling led to a בכור being slaughtered. It asks whether this unattributed משנה follows רבי מאיר alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if someone who is not an expert examined a בכור and it was slaughtered because of his ruling, it must be buried, and he pays from his own money. Shall we say this unattributed משנה follows רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and asks if it matches only the view of רבי מאיר. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 1 we saw that רבי מאיר forbids a בכור slaughtered on a non-expert's word as a קנס. This משנה gives the same ruling with no name attached. That suggests the משנה sides with רבי מאיר, which would be a big claim, since an unnamed משנה is usually taken as the accepted law.

keyTerms.meaning: An expert qualified to judge blemishes
A firstborn animal, which belongs to the כהן
It must be buried, meaning it is forbidden to eat
An unattributed, anonymous teaching
Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion the גמרא is testing

phrases.english: One who is not an expert,

phrases.aramaic: וְרָאָה אֶת הַבְּכוֹר וְנִשְׁחַט עַל פִּיו,
phrases.english: and he examined the firstborn, and it was slaughtered on his word,
that animal must be buried,
and he must pay from his own property.
Shall we say we learned the unattributed teaching like רבי מאיר?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the conclusion of step 1 (רבי מאיר's ruling is a קנס) to the anonymous משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the anonymous משנה follows only רבי מאיר

steps.title: Maybe the משנה is about eye films, where everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the משנה follows only רבי מאיר. The משנה may be talking about a blemish on the eye that changes after death, and in that case everyone agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the משנה is talking about films on the eye, and then it is everyone's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and says the משנה does not have to follow רבי מאיר alone. It may be a special case that everyone agrees with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A film on the eye can change after the animal dies (steps 2-5), so no one can check later whether the blemish was real. In that case even the חכמים agree the animal must be buried. So the משנה can be read as everyone's view, not just רבי מאיר's.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, used to suggest another reading
Films or blemishes on the eye
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about the non-expert can be read as everyone's opinion, because it may be talking about an eye blemish that cannot be checked after death.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is about films on the eye,
phrases.notes: These are the eye films that can change after death, discussed just before in steps 2-5.

phrases.english: and it is everyone's opinion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 6 by narrowing the משנה's case
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה must follow רבי מאיר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be set in a case of changing eye films, where the חכמים agree too

steps.title: How much the non-expert pays
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the one who pays pays a quarter of the value of a small animal and half of the value of a large animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: when he pays, he pays a quarter for a small animal and half for a large animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the actual amount the non-expert pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said he pays but not how much. The ברייתא sets the amount: a quarter for a sheep or goat and half for a cow. The different amounts will be explained next.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter
Small animal, such as a sheep or goat
Large animal, such as a cow
Half

phrases.english: It was taught: When he pays,
he pays a quarter for a small animal,
and half for a large animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail on the payment mentioned in the משנה quoted in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Payment is a quarter of a small animal's value and half of a large animal's value

steps.title: Why the difference between small and large animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the different payment amounts.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a large animal gets half and a small one only a quarter. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems odd to use different fractions for the same kind of mistake. The גמרא wants the logic behind the ברייתא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a large animal gets half and a small one a quarter

steps.title: רב פפא: a large loss compared to a small loss
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that losing a large animal is a big loss, while losing a small animal is a small loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: this one is a large loss, and that one is a small loss.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that the payment follows how big the loss is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cow is worth much more than a sheep, so losing it hurts the כהן more. That is why the ברייתא gives a bigger fraction for the large animal.

keyTerms.meaning: A large loss
A small loss

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
This is a large loss,
phrases.notes: "This" is the large animal, and "that" in the next line is the small animal.

phrases.english: and that is a small loss.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: זֶה הֶפְסֵד מְרוּבֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fraction depends on the size of the loss

steps.title: Then he should pay the actual loss
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: if the payment depends on the loss, he should simply pay the amount actually lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let him pay according to the loss!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's reason. If loss is the measure, why use fixed fractions at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A large animal is already worth more, so even the same fraction would give a bigger payment for it. If the goal is to match the loss, the payment should just follow the real loss, not two different fractions.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
According to the loss

phrases.english: If so, let him pay according to the loss!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reason that the fraction depends on the size of the loss
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If loss is the measure, the payment should simply match the real loss, without different fractions

steps.title: The small-animal payment was lowered because of the decree on raising small livestock
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר מנוח, in the name of רב אחא בר איקא, explains that the חכמים adjusted the payment for small animals because of the decree against raising small livestock.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר מנוח said in the name of רב אחא בר איקא: because of the decree against those who raise small animals, they touched it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the payment for small animals was lowered for a special reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real reason for the quarter is not just the size of the loss. It is tied to the decree against raising small livestock in ארץ ישראל, so the חכמים reduced the payment for small animals to a quarter.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree
Those who raise small livestock
They touched it, meaning the חכמים adjusted the amount

steps.whatToRemember: The non-expert pays half for a large animal and only a quarter for a small one. The lower amount for small animals is tied to the decree against raising small livestock.

phrases.english: רב הונא בר מנוח said
in the name of רב אחא בר איקא:
Because of the decree against those who raise small livestock,
they touched it.
phrases.notes: "Touched it" means the חכמים stepped in and lowered the payment for small animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם גְּזֵירַת מְגַדְּלֵי בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה נָגְעוּ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the small-animal amount
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fractions were set only by the size of the loss, so they should simply match the real loss
steps.terutzMaskana: The quarter for small animals comes from a rabbinic adjustment tied to the decree against raising small livestock

steps.title: A judge who rules wrongly pays, unless he is a court-approved expert
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that if a judge makes a mistake in a money case or a purity case, his ruling stands and he pays from his own money. A judge who is an expert approved by the court does not pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he judged a case and declared the guilty party innocent or the innocent party guilty, or declared something pure to be impure or something impure to be pure, what he did is done, and he pays from his own money. If he was an expert for the court, he is exempt from paying.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It moves from a mistaken ruling about a בכור to any judge's mistaken ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is not undone. Instead, the judge covers the loss he caused. A judge who was an approved expert of the court is exempt, just like the expert in the case of the בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה, introducing the text of a משנה
Declared the guilty party innocent
Declared something pure to be impure
What he did is done, meaning the ruling stands
An expert approved by the court
Exempt

steps.confusionAlert: "What he did is done" does not mean the judge was right. The ruling stays in place, but the judge still has to pay for the loss.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If he judged a case,

phrases.aramaic: זִיכָּה אֶת הַחַיָּיב וְחִיֵּיב אֶת הַזַּכַּאי,
phrases.english: declared the liable party exempt or the innocent party liable,

phrases.aramaic: טִימֵּא אֶת הַטָּהוֹר וְטִיהֵר אֶת הַטָּמֵא —
phrases.english: declared the pure impure or the impure pure,
what he did is done,
and he must pay from his own property.
And if he was an expert for the court,
he is exempt from paying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה that widens the topic from the בכור to any mistaken ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge who rules wrongly pays from his own money, but an expert approved by the court is exempt
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets the basic rule for a judge's personal responsibility for mistakes. The expert exemption will be the focus of the discussion that follows.

steps.title: Does the משנה follow only רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that our משנה, which makes a mistaken judge pay, must follow רבי מאיר, who holds people liable for indirect damage (דינא דגרמי).
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Shall we say that the unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר, who makes a person pay for damage he caused indirectly?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wonders whether our משנה must follow the opinion of רבי מאיר alone. A judge's ruling seems to cause damage only indirectly, and רבי מאיר is the one who holds people liable for that kind of damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A judge only speaks; the money moves because people follow his words. Making someone pay for damage like that is דינא דגרמי, which is רבי מאיר's view. If that is the only way to explain the משנה, then an unnamed משנה follows a single opinion, and the גמרא wants to avoid that.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say (introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test)
An unnamed, unattributed ruling in a משנה
Liability for damage caused indirectly

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ לֵימָא תְּנַן סְתָמָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: Gemara: Shall we say we learned the unattributed mishna like Rabbi Meir,
who rules liability for indirectly caused damage?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה from step 13 about a judge who errs.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a mistaken judge pays from his own money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A judge's ruling causes loss only indirectly, so making him pay seems to fit only רבי מאיר's view of דינא דגרמי.

steps.title: The judge handed it over with his own hand
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא in the name of רב explains that the משנה is talking about a judge who physically took the item from one side and gave it to the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said in the name of רב: The case is where the judge himself took the item and handed it over.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the משנה is talking about a judge who personally took the money or item and gave it to the other person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the judge moves the item with his own hands, the damage is direct, not גרמי. So the משנה can fit everyone, not only רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Took and gave with his hand: the judge physically moved the item
For example, in a case where

steps.confusionAlert: Here נשא ונתן does not mean 'did business' or 'debated.' It means the judge physically took the item and gave it away.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said that Rav said:
For example, where he took and gave with his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא אָמַר רַב כְּגוֹן שֶׁנָּשָׂא וְנָתַן בַּיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by narrowing the case to direct damage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The judge only spoke, so the damage was indirect and the משנה needs רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The judge physically transferred the item, so the damage is direct and everyone agrees he pays.

steps.title: How can wrongly exempting someone be done by hand?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts רב's answer for a judge who wrongly makes someone pay. It then asks how a judge who wrongly lets someone off could have physically handed anything over.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense when he wrongly obligated an innocent person: he took from him and gave by hand. But when he wrongly exempted the guilty person, how does that work? If he just told him 'You are exempt,' then he did not take and give by hand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב's answer. It works when the judge wrongly makes someone pay, but not when he wrongly lets someone off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the judge exempts someone, nothing changes hands. He just says 'you don't owe.' So רב's 'took and gave by hand' does not seem to fit that part of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense when... (sets up a contrast)
He obligated the innocent party
He exempted the liable party
What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: It works well when he obligated the innocent party —
for example, where he took and gave by hand,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא זִיכָּה אֶת הַחַיָּיב הֵיכִי דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: but when he exempted the liable party, what is the case?
If he said to him 'You are exempt' —
but he did not take and give by hand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 15's answer for one of the cases in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's explanation that the judge took and gave by hand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When a judge exempts someone, nothing is physically transferred, so the explanation cannot cover this case.

steps.title: He took back the security item
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that the lender was holding a security item (משכון), and the judge took it away from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The case is where the lender held a security item, and the judge took it from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא shows how exempting someone can also involve a physical act. The judge took a security item (משכון) away from the lender and returned it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender was already holding something to guarantee the loan. By physically taking it from him, the judge directly caused the lender's loss. That makes it direct damage just like the first case.

keyTerms.meaning: A security item held by a lender to guarantee a debt

phrases.english: Ravina said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ מַשְׁכּוֹן וּנְטָלוֹ הֵימֶנּוּ.
phrases.english: For example, where he had a security item and he took it from him.
phrases.notes: 'He' who had the item is the lender. The judge took it from him and gave it back to the borrower.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ מַשְׁכּוֹן וּנְטָלוֹ הֵימֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Exempting someone involves only words, so there is no direct act.
steps.terutzMaskana: The judge physically took a משכון from the lender, so the loss is direct.

steps.title: Direct acts in the purity cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the purity cases the same way. The judge touched pure food to a שרץ, or he mixed impure food into the owner's pure produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: He declared a pure item impure: he made it touch a שרץ. He declared an impure item pure: he mixed it with the owner's produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes applying רב's idea of direct action to the two purity cases in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case the judge did something physical that caused the loss. Touching food to a שרץ actually makes it impure. Mixing impure food into pure produce ruins the whole batch once the truth comes out. So in every case of the משנה the damage is direct, not גרמי.

keyTerms.meaning: He declared a pure item impure
He declared an impure item pure
A creeping creature whose dead body makes things impure
He mixed them

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, the judge in our משנה pays because he caused the loss directly with his own hands in every case. So the משנה does not need to follow רבי מאיר's view of דינא דגרמי.

phrases.english: He declared the pure impure —
where he made a creeping creature touch them,
he declared the impure pure —
where he mixed them with his produce.
phrases.notes: 'His produce' means the owner's pure produce. Mixing the impure food in spoils all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: טִימֵּא אֶת הַטָּהוֹר דְּאַגַּע בְּהוּ שֶׁרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the direct-action explanation from the money cases to the purity cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the same narrowing to the remaining cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In purity rulings the judge only speaks, so any loss is indirect.
steps.terutzMaskana: The judge physically touched the food to a שרץ or mixed it, so the loss is direct.

steps.title: The story of רבי טרפון and the cow
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה tells of a cow whose womb was removed. Because of רבי טרפון's ruling it was fed to dogs, and later the חכמים in יבנה permitted such a cow.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There was an incident with a cow whose womb was removed. רבי טרפון fed it to dogs. The case came before the חכמים in יבנה, and they permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a real-life story about a mistaken ruling. It is connected to the earlier rule about judges who err.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון treated the cow as forbidden, so it was thrown to the dogs. The חכמים in יבנה ruled that a cow like this is permitted. That means his ruling was a mistake that caused a real loss, and the question of whether he must pay is about to come up.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (a new משנה begins here)
An incident, a real event
The womb
The city where the main court of the חכמים sat
They permitted it

steps.whyThisMatters: This story is a real example of the earlier rule. It sets up whether a great sage who rules by mistake must pay for the loss.

phrases.english: Mishna: And there was an incident with a cow
whose womb was removed,
phrases.notes: הָאֵם here means the womb, not 'the mother.'

phrases.english: and Rabbi Tarfon fed it to dogs,
and the incident came before the Sages in Yavne,
and they permitted it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּפָרָה שֶׁנִּיטְּלָה הָאֵם שֶׁלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה that continues the theme of a judge's mistaken ruling from step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cow whose womb was removed is permitted. רבי טרפון's ruling that led to it being fed to dogs was a mistake.

steps.title: The doctor's report from Alexandria
steps.stepSummary: תודוס the doctor reports that cows and pigs leave Alexandria only after their wombs are cut out, so that they cannot give birth elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: And תודוס the doctor said: No cow or pig leaves Alexandria in Egypt unless they first cut out its womb, so that it will not give birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the story of the cow without a womb. A doctor reports that in Alexandria this surgery is done all the time and the animals keep living.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an animal can live a normal life after its womb is removed, then removing the womb does not make it a טריפה. This is real-world evidence that the חכמים in יבנה were right to permit such a cow, and that רבי טרפון's ruling was a mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: תודוס the doctor
Alexandria in Egypt
they cut
literally 'the mother'; here it means the womb
so that it will not give birth

phrases.english: And Todos the doctor said:
No cow or pig goes out
from Alexandria of Egypt
without their cutting out its womb,
so that it will not give birth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from step 19 and backs up the ruling of the חכמים in יבנה with evidence from real life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals whose wombs are removed keep living, so removing the womb does not make an animal a טריפה.

steps.title: רבי טרפון fears he must pay, and רבי עקיבא exempts him
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון thinks he will have to pay for the cow he wrongly sent to the dogs. רבי עקיבא tells him that an expert judge of the court is exempt from paying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון said: Your donkey is gone, טרפון! רבי עקיבא said to him: רבי טרפון, you are an expert for the court, and anyone who is an expert for the court is exempt from paying.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון realizes his ruling was wrong and fears he must pay the owner for the lost cow. רבי עקיבא calms him with a rule: an expert judge does not pay for his mistakes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the earlier steps about a judge who makes a mistake. Normally a judge who physically causes a loss may have to pay. An approved expert of the court, however, is exempt. That is רבי טרפון's status.

keyTerms.meaning: your donkey is gone; you will have to sell it to pay
an expert approved by the court or the public to judge
exempt from paying

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that an approved expert judge does not pay for a wrong ruling. The גמרא examines it in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon said:
Your donkey is gone, Tarfon!
phrases.notes: He is talking to himself. He thinks he will have to sell his donkey to pay the owner back for the cow.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him: Rabbi Tarfon,
you are an expert for the court,
and anyone who is an expert for the court
is exempt from paying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן: הָלְכָה חֲמוֹרְךָ טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the doctor's report shows the ruling was wrong, the משנה deals with whether רבי טרפון must pay.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An expert judge of the court who rules wrongly is exempt from paying for the loss.

steps.title: Why not say the ruling was simply cancelled?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא needed the expert-judge rule. רבי טרפון went against a משנה, and a ruling that goes against a משנה is cancelled anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But let him get the answer from a different rule: רבי טרפון made a mistake about something written in a משנה, and when a judge makes a mistake about something in a משנה, his ruling is reversed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא's reason. There seems to be a simpler and stronger reason why רבי טרפון does not pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a ruling goes against a clear משנה, it is cancelled and has no force. The owner should not have relied on it, so the loss is his own fault. Why bring in the expert-judge rule at all?

keyTerms.meaning: but let him derive it from (a different reason)
made a mistake about a clear rule written in a משנה
the ruling is reversed or cancelled

steps.confusionAlert: 'חוֹזֵר' here does not mean the judge changes his mind. It means the ruling itself is cancelled, as if it never happened.

phrases.english: Gemara
But let him derive it
from the fact that he erred in a matter of the Mishnah,
phrases.notes: The rule that a cow without a womb is kosher is written in a משנה (חולין 54a).

phrases.english: and one who erred in a matter of the Mishnah, the ruling is reversed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason רבי עקיבא gave in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's use of the rule that an expert judge is exempt from paying.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a more basic reason: a ruling against a clear משנה is cancelled, so the owner caused his own loss. The expert-judge rule should not be needed.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא gave two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא meant two reasons. First, the ruling went against a משנה and is cancelled. Second, even if the mistake was only in judgment, an expert judge is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is saying one reason and then another. One: a judge who makes a mistake about a משנה has his ruling cancelled. And another: even if your mistake was only in weighing the arguments, you are an expert for the court, and any expert for the court is exempt from paying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. רבי עקיבא did know the 'mistake against a משנה' reason; he added the expert-judge reason as a second layer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of mistakes. A mistake against a clear משנה cancels the ruling. A mistake in judgment, where a judge decides between opinions wrongly, does not cancel it. רבי עקיבא was saying that even if רבי טרפון's mistake counts only as the second kind, he still does not pay, because he is an approved expert.

keyTerms.meaning: he is saying one reason, and another besides
even if; or alternatively
weighing the arguments; a mistake in judgment, not against a clear source

steps.whatToRemember: A ruling that goes against a clear משנה is cancelled. Even when the mistake was only in judgment, an approved expert judge (מומחה לבית דין) is exempt from paying.

phrases.english: He is saying one reason and another:
One: one who erred in a matter of the Mishnah, the ruling is reversed,

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד — אִי נָמֵי בְּשִׁיקּוּל הַדַּעַת טָעִיתָה,
phrases.english: and another: even if you erred in weighing the arguments,
you are an expert for the court,
and anyone who is an expert for the court
is exempt from paying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the statement as two reasons, one on top of the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that רבי עקיבא relied only on the expert-judge rule and ignored the simpler 'mistake against a משנה' rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא meant both: the ruling is cancelled because it went against a משנה, and even if the mistake was only in judgment, an expert judge is exempt from paying.

steps.title: A paid examiner of firstborn animals must be an expert
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that one may not slaughter a בכור on the ruling of someone who takes payment to examine firstborn animals, unless he is a מומחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a person takes payment to be the one who checks firstborn animals, we do not slaughter a firstborn on his ruling, unless he was an expert.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a ruling about a person who gets paid to check firstborn animals for blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור may be slaughtered only after someone checks it and rules that it has a blemish. This משנה says that when the examiner takes payment for the job, we cannot slaughter the animal on his ruling. The one exception it gives here is when he is a מומחה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who takes payment
Firstborn animals
Based on his word or ruling
An expert

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who takes payment
to be one who examines the firstborn animals —
we may not slaughter on his ruling,
unless he was an expert.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַנּוֹטֵל שָׂכָר לִהְיוֹת רוֹאֶה אֶת הַבְּכוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story about רבי טרפון and the expert judge, a new משנה opens about paid examiners of firstborn animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not slaughter a בכור on the ruling of a paid examiner unless he is a מומחה.
